Author: topstockalerts
Text: Jim Cramer said Wall Street may be overreacting to the threat posed by Meta’s Muse AI agent to consumer companies, creating potential opportunities among stocks that have been broadly sold off. The so-called “consumer inertia” trade assumes AI agents could hurt businesses that benefit when customers fail to cancel subscriptions, compare prices or shop around for better deals. Since Muse launched Sept. 8, Planet Fitness has fallen 20%, while Airbnb and Booking Holdings are down 13% and 16%, respectively. SiriusXM has dropped about 11%, Charles Schwab 9% and Life Time 7%. Cramer argued that investors should assess each company’s actual exposure to AI rather than treating entire industries as potential losers. He pointed to Life Time as an example, saying its highly engaged members may be less likely to cancel than Planet Fitness customers. In travel, Cramer said online agencies retain value through features such as rewards programs and easy price comparisons. $META

Text: AI executives clashed with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei during a White House meeting, exposing divisions over AI safety and regulation. According to The Wall Street Journal, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang challenged Amodei over his warnings about AI risks, while Amodei defended greater transparency regarding cyber threats and potential labor-market disruption. The dispute reflects broader opposition to industry rules that could slow growth or concentrate regulatory power.
